top_choice_rationale: P001 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) credits one coherent, jointly authored body of design-based evidence on how import competition and technological change reshape labour demand, wages and local adjustment. The designs are transparent, have been replicated in other countries and refined rather than overturned, and the lesson about concentrated, persistent adjustment costs is general. Dorn is a full co-author of the central papers, so the three-name attribution is accurate. The citation should claim credible evidence on adjustment, not settled welfare magnitudes or origination of the task framework. The main costs are that the long-run skill-premium framing is left out and that the China-shock papers are younger than the other candidates' work. I judge these acceptable. P002 (BLP) ranks second because of its durability and use in practice, but it is mainly a method and excludes Bresnahan and Reiss. P003 (the Katz variant) is a coherent version of the same achievement. P004 has less well-identified cross-country evidence and a weaker Besley attribution. Any of the four awards is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: No connection to Autor, Dorn or Hanson is apparent from the profile. My co-authors listed there (Asplund, Steen, Ulsaker, Grönqvist, Wilander, Syverson, Goldstein) are not on P001. My field of industrial organisation is adjacent to P002, which I rank second. I co-authored with committee chair Hassler and former chair Ellingsen (IJIO 2026). Hassler supports the same P001 configuration, so I do not treat that agreement as independent evidence. I am an SSE colleague of Andersson, Dreber Almenberg and Strömberg, which is a tie between members and not to any candidate. My spouse is Magdalena Andersson, a former Swedish prime minister, a public fact with no apparent bearing on any proposal.
